# Native 3D picture outline joins

Original OPC/XML variants generated by `tools/picture_3d_joins_fixture.py` from
our authored four-color picture fixture. No corpus content or third-party engine
is used. Fourteen pages pair orthographic flat and perspective extruded rectangles
with absent/round joins, miter limits 800000/100000/omitted, square caps and empty
saved sketch metadata. Line width is 8 pt throughout.

`native.pdf` was exported by the reference application using
`tools/export-reference.ps1`. The source passes transitional schemas.
`tools/picture_3d_joins_reference.py` records source/PDF SHA-256 hashes, 1,844
native color samples with uniform one-point neighborhoods, full silhouettes,
and exact cropped-image comparisons. All fourteen
picture regions were visually inspected in a contact sheet.

Observed behavior:

- Flat absent/round joins have rounded outer corners; miter 800000 and omitted
  miter limits produce sharp corners.
- An extruded rectangle already has sharp corners for absent/round joins.
- Miter 100000 clips corners in both flat and extruded cases.
- Square versus flat caps produce identical closed-picture regions here.
- An empty sketch type with the saved empty geometry produces identical regions
  to the corresponding miter/square-cap control. This does not establish behavior
  for active sketch types or arbitrary saved geometry.

The XSD defines `CT_LineJoinMiterProperties.lim` as `ST_PositivePercentage`.
The integer spelling uses thousandths of a percent. These controls distinguish
join geometry and neutral metadata; they do not yet establish every miter-limit
threshold, geometry, camera, lighting or extension combination.

Import and rendering now support these controls. The browser compares every
native color sample and both directions of silhouette distance, then exercises
editing, original-part preservation, exact undo and export/reopen. Color samples
exclude antialiased edges; silhouettes independently cover those edges within
1.25 pt, the existing native 3D comparison tolerance.

The low-limit extruded control distinguishes the reference application's open diagonal side faces
from a closed octagonal prism; the clipped mesh also culls back faces. The
original no-join/round path is unchanged. Beveled 3D surfaces combined with
clipped joins remain guarded, and active sketch styles retain their existing
read-only behavior. Ordinary 2D outlines also preserve validated neutral cache
metadata through the same reader. This does not complete source #249, whose
next strict-import blocker is subscript formatting on an anchored group (the
existing guard currently rejects script formatting on all pictures).
